## A note before you start

This book pulls together what trusted baking sources agree on [S1]. Every source is numbered, so you can check it yourself.

## Chapter 1: Start Here

> The short version: A loaf is flour, water, salt and time [S1].

### How to use this book

Read one chapter, then bake. Short and simple wins.

| Say this | Not that |
|---|---|
| My starter is still learning | My starter is broken |

> Try tonight: Feed your starter and mark the jar with a band.

> Remember:
> - Flour, water, salt, time.
> - Warm kitchens go faster.
> - Write down what you did.

> Facts:
>
> - 1 to 2 weeks | is how long a new starter often takes [S2]
> - Salt slows fermentation a little [S1]

## Chapter 2: Folding in flavour

> The short version: Add mix-ins at the last fold so the dough stays strong [S2].

### When to add them

> Stat: 20% | of the flour weight is a common cap for mix-ins [S2]

> Steps:
> 1. **Laminate.** Stretch the dough thin on a wet bench.
> 2. **Scatter.** Spread the mix-ins evenly.
> 3. **Roll.** Fold it back up and rest it.

> Try tonight: Fold in a handful of cheese and see how it bakes.

> Remember:
> - Last fold, not first.
> - Dry mix-ins hold up best.
> - Keep to about a fifth of the flour.

> Facts:
>
> - 20% of flour weight | is a common mix-in cap [S2]
> - Wet fillings can tear the dough [S2]
